components.gap: Partial. Identification is formally defined (def:p15-fe-properties), consistency is stated in its sampling sense, and the finite countermodels separate them. But efficiency has only a prose description of Fisher's large-sample probable-error comparison, with no definition carrying explicit model, sampling and regularity scope, and sufficiency is defined only for finite sample spaces, although Fisher's criterion as reconstructed concerns general (continuous) sampling laws. Duty: define efficiency (Fisher's large-sample comparison and its information benchmark) and sufficiency (a general dominated or conditional-law criterion, not only finite masses), each with explicit model, sampling and regularity scope, so that every estimate and theorem distinguishing identification, consistency, efficiency and sufficiency has that scope and no missing regularity is hidden.

Partial. The route reconstructs, each with stated scope: Fisher's binomial example, the coordinate transformation, a finite score/information bound, the sufficiency gap, the Cauchy location example, phase-averaged grouping corrections, normal Fourier harmonics, moment-existence conditions, the cell likelihood and Pearson discrepancy, and the aperiodic grouped-normal information expansion. Not reconstructed with exact regularity conditions: Fisher's asymptotic large-sample efficiency/information argument for the maximum-likelihood solution (pp. 328-332; only its premises are listed at fisher-estimation-and-regularity.tex 182-188, and only a finite analogue is proved); section 8, efficiency of moments for Pearson Type III (pp. 332-338); section 9, location and scaling of frequency curves (pp. 338-342); sections 10-11, Pearsonian curves and the near-normal region (pp. 342-356); section 12, the Poisson series (p. 359) and dilution-series estimation (pp. 363-366); and, by the route's own proof boundary (fisher-grouping-and-moments.tex 350-363), the fixed-grid information periodic remainder bound, grouped-MLE existence and limit, and goodness-of-fit calibration. Duty: reconstruct each of these selected estimation arguments of the held 1922 paper with exact model, sampling and regularity scope, keeping any later asymptotic reformulation used to repair a claim separate, so that no maximization is treated as a complete inferential guarantee and no missing regularity is hidden.
